\label {sol: underlying preorder of an ordered vector space is a partial order}We need to just show that it is antisymmetric; let $x,y \in V$ with $x \leq y$ and $y \leq x$. Then, we see that $y-x \in V^+$ and $x-y = -(y-x) \in V^+$. So, $y-x \in V^+ \cap (-V^+)$. Since this intersection is trivial, we see that $y-x = 0$ so $x = y$.
